description: Single source of truth for all numeric quality gates (self-review, rewrite limits, paragraph/unit word bounds, style-fingerprint compliance, voice rule-coverage/corpus minimums, typography). Edit here; every skill and agent references this file. Gemini model/thinking-budget defaults and retry policy are NOT read from here — they live in SPEC_DEFAULTS in plugins/academic-writer/mcp/gemini-server/src/gemini-client.ts (overridable per-project via profile.md), and the retry constants are hardcoded in that same file. The antiAi block was REMOVED in 0.9.0: nothing computed that score, so it was the drafting model rating its own unrevised draft, and it measured a flat maximum on every paragraph of a live 13-unit run while the auditor failed several of the same paragraphs. Anti-AI patterns are now writing guidance (write/references/anti-ai-patterns-*.md), not a scored gate; the auditor's VERDICT is the per-paragraph gate.

selfReview._comment: Articles scoring below 40/60 trigger researcher review before final output. 6 dimensions x 10 points each.

rewriteCycles._comment: Maximum number of times a paragraph can be rewritten before being included with [NEEDS REVIEW].

paragraph._comment: Soft word ceiling per paragraph. Introduction and conclusion paragraphs may exceed by wordCeilingIntroConclusionBonus words.

writerUnit._comment: Min/target/max word bounds for a 'writer unit' — the leaf-level chunk that gets exactly one section-writer subagent. Sections whose word count exceeds maxWords must be decomposed by the architect into multiple writer-unit subsections (an outline `units` array); adjacent subsections under minWords should be merged into one unit rather than left tiny.

styleFingerprint._comment: Per-dimension style compliance score. Below 7 triggers paragraph adjustment.

exemplars._comment: src/scripts/extract-voice-exemplars.py: how many real paragraphs from past-articles/ are shown to Gemini as few-shot voice examples, their word bounds, and at most maxPerFile per source article so no single paper dominates the voice. Measured 2026-09-15 on the author's finished Hebrew papers: mean paragraph 97-134 words, so 40-150 keeps typical body paragraphs and drops headings and footnote-length fragments (a whole-folder corpus reads shorter because course reflections pull the mean down). Gemini guidance: 2-5 examples; more rarely helps.

jevShadow._comment: Opt-in (sends change text to TypeSafe AI); flagScore was fitted 2026-09-19 on 177 Hebrew edits from one article, where every edit labelled low scored ≤ 1.13 and every edit labelled medium or high scored ≥ 1.96 (agreement with the copyeditor LLM, not accuracy); shadow only. Script: src/scripts/jev-risk-shadow.py.

proofread._comment: Proofread pipeline caps, enforced in src/workflows/proofread.js from args.thresholds (WRK-14). chunkWords bounds one finder chunk; the mechanical loop exits 'converged' after dryRounds consecutive rounds with no fresh change, or 'cap-reached' at maxPasses. refuteVotes lenses verify each candidate change and refuteMajority of them refuting DOWNGRADES it to applied:false with skipReason 'refuted' — it is never dropped from the output (proofread.js:14-18, :305). refuteBudgetPerChunk caps how many changes per chunk are sent for refute-verification at all. Verification is batched: each lens (language) or vote (mechanical) judges all of a chunk's budgeted changes in ONE call, so verify calls are refuteVotes per chunk regardless of finding count (a live run spent ~9.7M of 13.5M tokens when it was one call per change per lens); the budget now bounds how many changes one call must judge, and glyph-only mechanical changes (gershayim/geresh/whitespace) are upheld by code and spend none of it. Changes beyond the budget are carried with skipReason 'refute-budget-exhausted' — downgraded, never dropped — and the budget is spent highest-meaningRisk first.

citationFloor._comment: VER-18 absence gate, enforced by src/scripts/gate.py citation-floor. The per-paragraph auditor is a PRESENCE check — it verifies that claims which ARE cited are cited correctly, and is structurally blind to a paragraph that cites nothing. Absence needs its own counting gate, and the count is arithmetic, not judgement (TST-02). Only SECONDARY citations count toward the floor: primary sources stay inline in this field, so a raw citation count reads healthy on an article carrying almost no scholarly engagement. minSecondaryPer1000Words is the rate floor, minSecondaryTotal the absolute floor that keeps a very short article from passing on rate alone. The gate FAILS if EITHER floor is breached.

typography._comment: dashReplacement is the default em/en-dash fix convention used by detect-ai-typography.py (values: hyphen|comma|colon|remove); overridable via --dash-replacement. topFrequentTermsCount/minTermLength configure extract-style-metrics.py's frequentTerms extraction. furnitureMaxWords/furnitureShare/furnitureMinCount drop structural furniture (table-of-contents lines and section headers) from frequentTerms: a term is furniture when at least furnitureShare of its occurrences fall in paragraphs of at most furnitureMaxWords words and it occurs at least furnitureMinCount times. Calibrated on a real 10-file corpus of 857 paragraphs with a 38-word median: the author's own name sits in 5-word ToC lines and scores 96%, subject vocabulary scores 3%, and the highest-scoring term that is kept scores 73% — so the 0.8 cutoff has margin on both sides. Only terms in contention for the reported list are judged — the top topFrequentTermsCount * furnitureCandidateMultiplier by raw count — because a share computed over a handful of occurrences has no resolution: ב׳ and א׳, the same token doing the same job in the same two files, scored 0.80 and 0.50 on five and seven observations and split. Replaces a front-matter rule that inspected the first N paragraphs of each file and never fired, because these headers repeat throughout a document rather than opening it.

proofread._comment: Token ceiling comfortably covers a long proofread run; the USD ceiling is the primary cost guard.

write._comment: Token ceiling covers multi-section drafting; the USD ceiling is the primary cost guard.

voiceMoves._comment: One call to derive qualitative voice moves.

revise._comment: One bounded classification pass for author review items.

awImprove._comment: Development-only defect clustering and Jev roster thresholds.

_piModelNote: piModel = OpenRouter model for the isolated Pi judge. Must be a non-Claude, non-Gemini family (cross-family verification); taken from the author's Pi model roster (executor tier, machine-config/pi/model-roster.json). Runs in shadow until the Hebrew fixture shows parity.
